adjointCarlesonSum_adjoint.statement: Let $X$ be a metric space and work under the standing assumptions of the proof: the data $a\in\mathbb N$, $q\in\mathbb R$, $K:X\times X\to\mathbb C$, $\sigma_1,\sigma_2:X\to\mathbb Z$, $F,G\subseteq X$ of `ProofData` (making $X$ a doubling metric measure space with measure $\mu$), together with a tile structure `TileStructure Q (defaultD a) (defaultκ a) (defaultS X) (cancelPt X)` with set of tiles $\mathfrak P(X)$. Let $f,g:X\to\mathbb C$ be bounded with compact support and let $\mathfrak C\subseteq\mathfrak P(X)$ be a set of tiles. Then $$\int_X\overline{g(x)}\,T_{\mathfrak C}f(x)\,d\mu(x)=\int_X\overline{T^*_{\mathfrak C}g(x)}\,f(x)\,d\mu(x),$$ where $T_{\mathfrak C}$ is `carlesonSum` and $T^*_{\mathfrak C}$ is `adjointCarlesonSum`, i.e. $T^*_{\mathfrak C}$ is the adjoint of $T_{\mathfrak C}$.
